title: api: standardize Retry-After + idempotency semantics for streaming and OpenAI-compat endpoints
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: clients integrating via the OpenAI-compat layer reported inconsistent retry behavior for rate-limited streaming requests and ambiguous idempotency semantics for long-running streaming calls. This PR unifies Retry-After semantics across REST and streaming endpoints, formalizes idempotency key handling for streaming requests, and returns consistent machine-readable error payloads. Summary of changes: 1) Add standardized Retry-After headers (seconds and RFC1123 fallback) for 429 responses; 2) Implement server-side idempotency middleware for streaming endpoints: requests with the same Idempotency-Key + identical critical parameters will dedupe or return the previously completed result; concurrently running requests return 409 with idempotency status; 3) Define and return stable error codes in JSON (error.code and error.message) across OpenAI-compat and native endpoints (examples: rate_limit_exceeded, idempotency_conflict, invalid_request, internal_error); 4) Streaming protocol: when a streaming connection is interrupted, clients can retry with the same Idempotency-Key; server will either resume (if state persisted and resumeSupported flag true) or return the terminal result/duplicate detection; 5) Add tests, integration harness updates, and docs in the OpenAI-compat reference. Compatibility notes: behavior is backwards-compatible for clients that do not send Idempotency-Key; clients should start sending Idempotency-Key for long-running streams to get dedup/resume guarantees. Migration: operator-facing rollout gated behind a feature flag for 2 weeks, can be toggled per-region. See related Linear items ENG-1245 and ENG-1301 for rollout plan and metrics.
